newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares higher at noon, properties shine.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares higher at noon, properties shine.

text.p: Singapore shares were broadly higher at noon on Tuesday with property stocks rising sharply.
Some dealers said the sharp gains in properties were unexpected given the uncertain outlook in the Singapore property market.
"A lot of people still don't like properties because of the weak outlook. But some investors obviously have a different view on property prices and interest rates," said one dealer.
The SES property index was up 2.76 percent, or 18.53 points, to 689.33. Keppel Land was among the top gainers in active dealings, rising almost eight percent or 30 cents to S$4.18.
The Straits Times Industrial index rose 28.77 points to 2,057.37. Total market volume was 102.5 million shares with 275 gainers against 52 losers.
Dealers said new issues found renewed interest. "Many of these issues came out at a time when the market was down and did not perform. But now they seem to be back in favour," said one.

Among them, disk-drive components maker MMI Holdings topped the actives with more than eight million shares traded. It touched rose to S$0.72, up 6.5 cents at noon. Raffles Medical also touched a new high of S$0.63 in active trading.
